title: Sodom and the Son of Promise, part 4 of 6: Abraham Tested on the Mountain
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The age of the patriarchs in the ancient Near East, about four thousand years ago: people dressed in simple garments of wool or linen, undyed or dyed in earth colours, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

ABRAHAM.name: Abraham
ABRAHAM.desc: Abraham, a tall, upright old man who looks about eighty and is still strong, with warm brown, deeply weathered and lined skin, thick wavy white hair reaching his collar, a full white beard, white eyebrows, a strong straight nose and steady, thoughtful dark eyes, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool with a brown leather belt and a deep russet-red wool mantle draped over his left shoulder, and simple leather sandals

ISAAC.name: Isaac
ISAAC.desc: Isaac, a sturdy, well-grown youth of about fifteen, beardless, with warm brown skin, an open oval face with round cheeks, large dark eyes, a straight nose and thick curly dark-brown hair that covers his ears, wearing a knee-length short-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool with a thin red-and-blue woven cord tied at the waist, and simple leather sandals

blocks.TWOMEN: Exactly two men in the picture, no one else
blocks.GCAMP: Abraham's camp in the south country: several low, wide tents of black goat-hair cloth pitched on dry, gently rolling grassland of pale gold grass beside a broad dry stream bed of pale gravel with a few feathery tamarisk trees; no oak trees, no walls, no buildings
blocks.INTENT: inside a wide tent of black goat-hair cloth, with wooden poles, woven rugs on the ground, cushions and striped wool blankets, lit by one small clay oil lamp burning with a single flame
blocks.WELL: a desert well: a low ring of rough piled stones about knee high around a dark round shaft, with a worn stone trough beside it
blocks.NOTOWN: The background is only open grassland, the dry stream bed and sky: no walls, no houses, no town, no flags and no ruins
blocks.SKYLIGHT: from high in the open sky a great shaft of pure golden-white light breaks straight down onto the mountain top, with no figure, no face, no wings and no human shape anywhere in the light or in the sky
blocks.SERVANTS: two young men, servants of the household: the first is tall and thin with a short black beard and a brown cloth head wrap, in a knee-length tunic of rough brown wool; the second is shorter and broad-shouldered, beardless, with cropped black hair, in a knee-length tunic of rough grey wool; each carries a plain wooden staff
blocks.DONKEY: a small grey donkey with a pale muzzle and a dark stripe along its back, saddled with folded brown wool blankets tied on with rope, with a plain rope halter
blocks.WOOD: a bundle of split firewood, about a dozen rough-split pale logs as long as a man's arm, bound together with two turns of rope
blocks.EMBERPOT: a small round clay firepot hanging from a short rope handle, with embers glowing dull orange at its mouth
blocks.KNIFE: a plain knife with a short, leaf-shaped blade of dull bronze and a smooth wooden handle
blocks.HILLS: dry limestone hill country: rounded hills of pale grey rock and thin golden grass, dotted with olive-green scrub and a few gnarled trees, under a wide sky
blocks.MOUNT: the top of a mountain in the land of Moriah: a bare, rounded summit of pale grey limestone and thin dry grass, with thorny scrub at its edges and ranges of empty hills fading into blue haze far below
blocks.ALTAR: a low altar of rough, unhewn field stones piled waist high and about as long as a man, with split firewood laid in neat rows on top of it
blocks.RAM: a full-grown white ram with big, heavy, curled horns on both sides of its head, clearly a ram, not a lamb and not a ewe
blocks.NOBUILD: The background is only bare hills and sky: no tents, no walls, no buildings, no towns, no flocks, no jars
blocks.COURT: the courtyard of a flat-roofed house of tan mud brick, with a wooden door, clay water jars, a wooden ladder to the roof and a wide green northern plain seen over the low courtyard wall; no domes, no arches, no columns
blocks.NAHOR: Nahor, Abraham's brother, a stout old man with warm brown skin, a round face, short white hair and a broad white beard, wearing an ankle-length tunic of blue-grey wool with a fringed tan wool shawl over one shoulder
blocks.MILCAH: Milcah, an old woman with warm brown skin, a heart-shaped face and curly grey hair under a saffron-yellow wool head shawl, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved dress of olive-green wool
blocks.TAMARISK: a tamarisk tree twice the height of a man, with a slender reddish-brown trunk and a soft crown of feathery grey-green foliage
blocks.FOUR: Exactly four people in the picture, no one else

segs.text: Some time later God tested Abraham and said to him,
“Abraham!”
“Here I am,”
he answered.
“Take your son,”
God said,
“your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains, which I will show you.”

So Abraham got up early the next morning, saddled his donkey, and took along two of his servants and his son Isaac. He split the wood for a burnt offering and set out for the place God had designated.
On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
“Stay here with the donkey,”
Abraham told his servants.
“The boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we will return to you.”
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac. He himself carried the fire and the sacrificial knife, and the two of them walked on together.
Then Isaac said to his father Abraham,
“My father!”
“Here I am, my son,”
he replied.
“The fire and the wood are here,”
said Isaac,
“but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”
Abraham answered,
“God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.”
And the two walked on together.
When they arrived at the place God had designated, Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac and placed him on the altar, atop the wood.
Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
Just then the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven,
“Abraham, Abraham!”
“Here I am,”
he replied.
“Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him,”
said the angel,
“for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your only son from me.”
Then Abraham looked up and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns. So he went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
And Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide. So to this day it is said,
“On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.”
And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time,
saying,
“By Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that because you have done this and have not withheld your only son,
I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the gates of their enemies.
And through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.”
Abraham went back to his servants, and they got up and set out together for Beersheba. And Abraham settled in Beersheba.
Some time later, Abraham was told,
“Milcah has also borne sons to your brother Nahor:
Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel (the father of Aram),
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
And Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah bore these eight sons to Abraham’s brother Nahor.
Moreover, Nahor’s concubine, whose name was Reumah, bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

stills.prompt: Character reference sheet of {ISAAC}: a full-body front view standing and a head-and-shoulders portrait, side by side, calm, open, trusting expression, plain warm-grey background. One person only, shown twice. He is a boy in his middle teens, not a child and not a grown man: no beard, no moustache. No staff, no tools, no bundle, empty hands. The plain warm-grey painted background fills the whole picture from edge to edge behind both views: no landscape, no sky, no ground plants, no buildings, no writing and no other people anywhere. The skin is the same warm brown in both views.

{EMPTY}. Night at Beersheba: several low, wide tents of black goat-hair cloth stand dark and asleep on dry grassland beside {WELL}, and {TAMARISK}, under {STARS}. No fire, no smoke, no lamp. Wide view.

God said to him, Abraham: night on open dry grassland outside the camp. {GLORY}, floods the grass in front of an old man. {ABRAHAM}, is seen from behind and a little to one side, small in the lower left of the picture, risen to his feet and looking up into the light. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {ONE}. No tents near him. Wide view.

Here I am: at night, a close view of the face of {ABRAHAM}, lifted toward a soft golden-white light that falls on him from above the frame, his eyes open and attentive, his lips just parted to answer. Dark sky behind him, nothing else. {ONE}. {NOHALO}. {NOEYES}. Close view of head and shoulders.

Your only son Isaac, whom you love: {INTENT}. {ISAAC}, lies peacefully asleep on his side on a woven rug under a striped wool blanket drawn up to his chest, one hand under his cheek, the lamplight warm on his face. {ONE}. Medium close view.

Take your son: night on open dry grassland. {ABRAHAM}, stands alone in a pool of golden-white light that falls from above the frame, his face stricken and still, his right hand gripping the edge of his mantle at his chest and his left hand hanging open at his side. Darkness and stars behind him. {ONE}. {NOHALO}. {NOEYES}. Medium view.

Go to the land of Moriah, to one of the mountains: {EMPTY}. Night. Range behind range of dark, bare, rounded limestone hills runs to the horizon under {STARS}, and far away the top of one distant hill is touched by a faint, pale golden light from above. No tents, no walls, no buildings, no fires. Very wide view.

Abraham got up early the next morning: in the grey light before sunrise, {ABRAHAM}, comes out of {TENT}, holding the door flap aside with one hand, his face grave and resolved after a sleepless night. {ONE}. Medium view.

He saddled his donkey: at first light on dry grassland, {ABRAHAM}, stands beside {DONKEY}, pulling tight with both hands the rope that holds the folded blankets on its back. The donkey stands quietly. {ONE}. One donkey only, no other animals. Medium view in side view.

He took along two of his servants and his son Isaac: at sunrise beside a black tent, {FOUR}. From left to right they are: {SERVANTS}, both standing ready and waiting; then {ISAAC}, tying the cord at his waist; then {ABRAHAM}, at the right, beckoning to them with one hand. Medium wide view.

He split the wood for a burnt offering: early morning on dry grassland, {ABRAHAM}, his mantle laid aside on the ground, stands with both hands on the wooden haft of a bronze-headed axe that has just bitten into a short log standing on a chopping block; pale split logs lie around his feet. {ONE}. No one watching, no animals. Medium view.

And set out for the place God had designated: sunrise over wide dry grassland. Seen from behind and far off, a small party walks away from us along a faint track toward distant pale hills: an old man in a russet-red mantle leading one grey donkey loaded with a bundle of split firewood, a youth in a cream tunic walking beside him, and two servants with staffs following. Exactly four tiny people and one donkey, all seen from behind. No tents, no other animals. Very wide view.

On the third day: midday in {HILLS}. Seen from the side and far off, a small party climbs a stony path from left to right: an old man in a russet-red mantle leading one grey donkey loaded with a bundle of split firewood, a youth in a cream tunic, and two servants with staffs. Exactly four tiny people and one donkey. {NOBUILD}. Very wide view.

Abraham looked up: in dry hill country, a close view of {ABRAHAM}, dusty from three days of walking, lifting his eyes to something far ahead and above him, one hand raised to shade his eyes from the sun, his face grave. Pale rock and sky behind him: no tents, no buildings, no animals. {ONE}. Close view of head and shoulders.

And saw the place in the distance: {EMPTY}. Beyond dry valleys and ridge after ridge of pale limestone hills, one bare, rounded mountain stands a little higher than the rest, blue-grey in the haze of the far distance under a wide morning sky. No tents, no walls, no buildings, no towns, no smoke. Very wide view.

Stay here with the donkey: in dry hill country, exactly three men and one donkey. At the right {ABRAHAM}, faces the other two and holds up his open right hand, palm toward them, telling them to stay. At the left stand {SERVANTS}, listening, the taller one holding the rope halter of {DONKEY}. {NOBUILD}. Medium wide view.

The boy and I will go over there to worship: in dry hill country, {ABRAHAM}, stands at the left with his right arm stretched out, pointing far away to a bare, rounded mountain blue in the distance, and beside him {ISAAC}, looks where he points. {MANBOY}. {NOBUILD}. Medium wide view from a little behind them.

And then we will return to you: under a single gnarled tree in dry hill country, exactly two men and one donkey. {SERVANTS}, have sat down on the ground in the tree's shade with their staffs across their knees, both looking away toward the right. Beside them stands {DONKEY}, tied to the tree. {NOBUILD}. Medium wide view.

Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac: in dry hill country, {ABRAHAM}, stands behind {ISAAC}, and with both hands settles {WOOD}, onto the youth's back, where it hangs from two rope loops over his shoulders. The youth leans forward a little to take the weight. {MANBOY}. {NOBUILD}. Medium view in side view.

The wood on his son Isaac: on a stony uphill path, {ISAAC}, walks from left to right bent forward under {WOOD}, carried on his back by two rope loops over his shoulders, both his hands gripping the ropes at his chest, his face set and willing. {ONE}. {NOBUILD}. Medium view in side view.

He himself carried the fire and the sacrificial knife: a very close view at waist height of an old man walking on a stony path. His weathered brown right hand carries {EMBERPOT}. Tucked under the brown leather belt of his long cream wool tunic, beside a fold of russet-red mantle, is {KNIFE}, in a plain leather sheath so that only its wooden handle shows. {HANDS}. No blood. Very close view.

And the two of them walked on together: seen from behind and below, two small figures climb a bare limestone slope toward a rounded summit against a pale sky: on the left an old man with white hair in a russet-red mantle carrying a small clay firepot, and on the right a youth in a cream tunic bent under a bundle of firewood on his back. Exactly two people, seen from behind, close together. {NOBUILD}. Wide view.

My father: on a bare mountain slope, a close view of {ISAAC}, seen from the chest up, with rope loops over his shoulders and the ends of split logs showing behind his head, turning his face to speak to someone just out of the picture on the right, his brow a little puzzled. Pale rock and sky behind him. {ONE}. Close view.

Here I am, my son: on a bare mountain slope, {ABRAHAM}, has stopped on the path and half turned to look back and down toward the left with deep tenderness, holding {EMBERPOT}, in his lowered right hand. {ONE}. {NOBUILD}. Medium view.

The fire and the wood are here: on a bare mountain slope, {ISAAC}, on the left, carrying a bundle of split firewood on his back, points with one hand at {EMBERPOT}, which hangs from the right hand of {ABRAHAM}, who stands on the right, looking at his son. {MANBOY}. No animals anywhere. {NOBUILD}. Medium view.

But where is the lamb for the burnt offering: {EMPTY}. A bare limestone mountainside of pale grey rock, thin dry grass and thorny scrub rising to an empty rounded summit under a wide sky. No sheep, no lambs, no goats, no animals of any kind, no birds, no tents, no buildings. Wide view.

God Himself will provide the lamb, my son: on a bare mountain slope, a close view of {ABRAHAM}, on the right, his eyes wet, laying his left hand on the shoulder of {ISAAC}, on the left, who looks up into his father's face, trusting. Both are seen from the chest up. {MANBOY}. Pale rock and sky behind them. Medium close view.

And the two walked on together: seen from the side and far off against a huge pale sky, two small figures walk from left to right along the bare crest of a limestone mountain, almost at its rounded summit: in front an old man with white hair in a russet-red mantle, and close behind him a youth in a cream tunic bent under a bundle of firewood on his back. Exactly two people. {NOBUILD}. Very wide view.

They arrived at the place God had designated: {MOUNT}. {ABRAHAM}, and {ISAAC}, stand side by side, small in the middle of the open summit, looking around them; {WOOD}, has been set down on the ground at the youth's feet. {MANBOY}. No altar yet, no tents, no buildings, no animals. Wide view.

Abraham built the altar there: on a bare limestone mountain top, {ABRAHAM}, his mantle laid aside, bends to set a heavy rough field stone with both hands on top of a low, half-built pile of unhewn stones about knee high. More loose stones lie about on the ground. No wood on the stones yet and no fire. {ONE}. {NOBUILD}. Medium view.

And arranged the wood: a very close view of an old man's weathered brown hands, in the sleeves of a cream wool tunic, laying a pale split log down beside others in a neat row on top of a low altar of rough, unhewn field stones. Bare mountain top and sky behind. {HANDS}. No fire, no smoke, no blood. Very close view.

He bound his son Isaac: a very close view of two pairs of hands. A youth's brown hands are held out together, wrists side by side, in front of his cream wool tunic, and an old man's weathered hands, coming from long sleeves of undyed cream wool with a fold of russet-red mantle behind them, wind a length of plain rope cord around the youth's wrists. The youth's hands are relaxed, lowered and do not resist; they are not raised in prayer. All the cloth in the picture is cream wool or russet-red wool: nothing blue, nothing green. {HANDS}. No knife, no blood. Very close view.

And placed him on the altar, atop the wood: {MOUNT}. In the middle of the summit stands {ALTAR}. On top of the wood {ISAAC}, lies on his back, fully clothed, his wrists tied together with rope cord and resting on his chest, his eyes open and looking up at the sky. Beside the altar stands {ABRAHAM}, his head bowed, one hand resting on his son's hair. {MANBOY}. No knife in the picture, no fire, no blood. Medium wide view in side view.

Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife: a very close view of an old man's weathered brown right hand, in the sleeve of a cream wool tunic, closing around the smooth wooden handle of {KNIFE}, which lies flat on a rough grey stone at the edge of an altar of unhewn stones, beside the ends of pale split logs. {HANDS}. The blade is clean: no blood. Very close view.

To slaughter his son: on a bare mountain top, a close view of the face of {ABRAHAM}, in anguish, his eyes shut tight, his brow deeply furrowed and his lips pressed together, his white hair blown by the wind. Only sky behind him. {ONE}. No knife in the picture. Close view of head and shoulders.

Abraham took the knife: seen from far off and from behind, very small and dark against a huge, pale, windy sky, one old man in a long mantle stands beside a low altar of piled stones on a bare mountain top, his head bowed and his right arm hanging straight down at his side. On the altar the shape of someone lying still on the wood is only just made out. Exactly one standing figure. His arm is lowered, not raised. {NOBUILD}. Very wide view.

Just then the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven: very wide view of a bare limestone mountain top under a great sky. {SKYLIGHT}. Far below, very small, one old man standing beside a low stone altar has thrown his head back to look straight up into the light. {NOLIGHTFIG}. No buildings, no tents. Very wide view.

Abraham, Abraham. Here I am: on a bare mountain top, a close view of {ABRAHAM}, his face thrown upward and flooded with golden-white light from above the frame, his eyes wide open and wet, his lips parted to answer. Only sky behind him. {ONE}. {NOHALO}. {NOEYES}. No knife in the picture. Close view of head and shoulders from a little below.

Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him: a very close view of rocky ground at the foot of an altar of rough stones, bathed in golden-white light from above. {KNIFE}, lies on the bare rock where it has fallen, and above it an old man's weathered brown right hand hangs open and empty, the fingers spread. {HANDS}. The blade is clean: no blood. Very close view.

For now I know that you fear God: on a bare mountain top, {ABRAHAM}, has sunk to his knees on the rocky ground beside the base of a low altar of rough stones, bowed forward with both hands flat on the ground and his head low, in a pool of golden-white light that falls from above the frame. Only the stones at the foot of the altar are seen at the edge of the picture. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOHALO}. Medium view.

You have not withheld your only son: a very close view of two pairs of hands in warm golden light. An old man's weathered hands are loosening and pulling away a length of plain rope cord from around a youth's brown wrists, which rest on his cream wool tunic; the cord is already half undone. {HANDS}. No knife, no blood. Very close view.

Then Abraham looked up and saw behind him: on a bare mountain top, {ABRAHAM}, kneeling on one knee, has twisted round to look back over his right shoulder at something behind him, his eyes widening in wonder. Thorny scrub at the edge of the summit behind him. {ONE}. {NOBUILD}. Medium view.

A ram in a thicket, caught by its horns: at the edge of a bare mountain top, {RAM}, stands alone in a dense thicket of dry, thorny brush, its two curled horns firmly tangled among the thick branches so that it cannot pull its head free. {NOPEOPLE}. Exactly one animal. Medium view.

So he went and took the ram: at the edge of a bare mountain top, {ABRAHAM}, bends into a thicket of dry, thorny brush and with both hands works the curled horns of {RAM}, free of the branches. {ONE}. Exactly one animal. No knife, no blood. Medium view.

And offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son: {MOUNT}, at evening. A strong fire burns on top of a low altar of rough, unhewn field stones, its flames and grey smoke rising straight up. A few steps from it {ABRAHAM}, stands with his arm around the shoulders of {ISAAC}, whose hands are free; both watch the fire. Nothing is seen in the fire but burning wood. {MANBOY}. No animal in the picture, no blood. Medium wide view.

In place of his son: on a bare mountain top at evening, in warm firelight from the left, {ABRAHAM}, holds {ISAAC}, tightly in both arms, the youth's face pressed against his father's shoulder and the old man's cheek resting on his son's curly hair, his eyes closed. Both are seen from the waist up. {MANBOY}. Medium close view.

And Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide: {MOUNT}, at evening. Beside a low altar of rough stones on which embers glow, {ABRAHAM}, stands with his face and both open hands lifted to the sky, speaking; beside him {ISAAC}, stands with his head bowed. {MANBOY}. {NOHALO}. No writing anywhere. Medium wide view from a little below.

On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided: {EMPTY}. Sunset. A bare, rounded limestone mountain top stands dark against a sky of gold and deep blue, and on it, small in the middle of the picture, a low altar of piled stones stands alone. Ranges of empty hills fall away below into dusk. No tents, no walls, no buildings, no writing. Very wide view.

And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time: very wide view at dusk of a bare limestone mountain top under a deep blue sky with the first stars. {SKYLIGHT}. Far below, very small, exactly two people stand side by side near a low stone altar, an old man and a youth, both looking straight up into the light. {NOLIGHTFIG}. No buildings, no tents. Very wide view.

By Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD: on a bare mountain top at dusk, {ABRAHAM}, and {ISAAC}, are seen from behind and a little to one side, standing close together in the lower part of the picture and looking up into {GLORY}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {MANBOY}. Wide view.

You have not withheld your only son: on a bare mountain top at dusk, a close view of {ISAAC}, his face lifted toward a golden-white light from above the frame, his eyes wide with awe; an old man's weathered hand rests on his shoulder at the edge of the picture. Only one face in the picture. {NOHALO}. His eyes are natural dark eyes and do not glow. Close view of head and shoulders.

I will surely bless you: at dusk on a bare mountain top, a close view of {ABRAHAM}, his face lifted into a soft golden-white light from above the frame, tears on his cheeks and the beginning of a smile of wonder. Deep blue sky behind him. {ONE}. {NOHALO}. {NOEYES}. Close view of head and shoulders.

I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky: {EMPTY}. Night. {STARS}, fills almost the whole picture above a low dark line of bare, rounded hills at the very bottom. No tents, no fires, no buildings. Very wide view looking up.

And the sand on the seashore: {EMPTY}. A wide, empty seashore in early light: a broad beach of pale golden sand runs from the very front of the picture, where the single grains can be seen, away to the far horizon, with a calm blue sea lapping gently at its edge on the right. No boats, no footprints, no buildings, no birds. Wide view from low to the ground.

Your descendants will possess the gates of their enemies. {VISION}. The great gateway of a walled city stands open, its two tall wooden doors swung wide between two square towers, and a long stream of tiny people walks in through it from the plain. No weapons raised, no fighting, no fire, no banners, no writing. Very wide view.

And through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed. {VISION}. A boundless plain crowded from the foreground to the far horizon with a countless multitude of tiny people of every kind, men, women and children, standing together with their faces turned toward a soft golden light that rises beyond the horizon. No buildings, no banners, no weapons, no writing. Very wide view from above.

Because you have obeyed My voice: on a bare mountain top at nightfall, {ABRAHAM}, stands with his head bowed and his right hand laid flat on his chest, the last of a golden-white light from above fading on his shoulders, the first stars behind him. {ONE}. {NOHALO}. Medium view.

Abraham went back to his servants: morning in dry hill country, under a single gnarled tree. In the foreground, seen from behind, {SERVANTS}, are getting to their feet beside one grey donkey, looking away up a stony slope, down which two small figures are coming toward them: an old man with white hair in a russet-red mantle and, a step behind him, a youth in a cream tunic. {FOUR}, and one donkey. {NOBUILD}. Wide view.

And they got up and set out together for Beersheba: evening light in {HILLS}. Seen from the side and far off, a small party walks from right to left down a stony path: an old man in a russet-red mantle and a youth in a cream tunic walking side by side in front, then two servants with staffs, one of them leading one grey donkey that carries only folded blankets. Exactly four tiny people and one donkey. {NOBUILD}. Very wide view.

And Abraham settled in Beersheba: in dry golden grassland beside {WELL}, {ABRAHAM}, sits on the ground in the shade of {TAMARISK}, resting his back against its trunk, his staff across his knees, looking out peacefully; a few black tents and grazing sheep lie behind in the distance. {ONE}. {NOTOWN}. Wide view.

Some time later, Abraham was told: in front of {TENT}, in dry grassland, {ABRAHAM}, sits on a woven rug at the right, listening closely to a traveller who stands before him at the left: a lean, dusty man of about thirty with a short black beard, a tan cloth head wrap and a knee-length tunic of faded blue-grey wool, leaning on a long staff with a water skin slung at his side, speaking with one hand lifted. {TWOMEN}. Medium wide view.

Milcah has also borne sons to your brother Nahor: far away in the north, in {COURT}, exactly two people sit side by side on a bench against the wall in afternoon light: on the left {NAHOR}, and on the right {MILCAH}, her hands folded in her lap. Exactly two people, one old man and one old woman, no one else. Medium wide view.

Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel: on a wide green northern plain with grazing sheep, exactly three grown men stand in a row facing us, brothers with warm brown skin and black hair. card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 22:1–24, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 22:1-24 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, G the voice of God (22:1-2), A Abraham, I Isaac (22:7), L the angel of the LORD (22:11-12, 22:16-18; same voice as G, as in s02e01d and s02e02c, a default that can be changed at assembly), T the unnamed person who brings the news of 22:20-22 ('Abraham was told'). The saying of 22:14 is spoken by the narrator. 22:12 'from me' is printed in lower case in the BSB.
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. REF = character reference sheet (not used in the film, no clip). Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

Faces: Abraham uses refs/REF-ABRAHAM.jpg from s02e01e with its description word for word. New sheet in this unit: refs/REF-ISAAC-YOUTH.jpg (key ISAAC), Isaac as a beardless youth of about fifteen. The text gives no age: he is called 'the boy' (22:5, 22:12) and is strong enough to carry the wood for a burnt offering up the mountain (22:6), so he is painted as a well-grown youth (I); readings run from a child to a man in his thirties and the picture does not settle it beyond what 22:6 requires. He keeps the cream tunic and the red-and-blue cord of the small Isaac of s02e02c (block CHILD there). Later units that need Isaac as a man of forty (Genesis 24-25) should derive a new sheet from this one.

God is light only (GLORY). 22:1-2: God speaks at night (the hour is I, from 22:3 'early the next morning'). The angel of the LORD who calls 'from heaven' (22:11, 22:15) is a shaft of light from the open sky (SKYLIGHT): no figure, face or wings; whether the angel is the LORD himself (he says 'from me' and 'By Myself I have sworn') or a messenger is not resolved on screen.

22:2 'the land of Moriah' is painted as bare limestone hill country with one rounded summit. No city, wall or building is shown and the mountain is not identified with any later site (2 Chronicles 3:1 names Mount Moriah as the temple hill; whether this is the same place is not decided on screen). 22:14: the name is spoken, never written in the picture.

22:3: the picture follows the verse's own order (rising, saddling, taking the servants and Isaac, splitting the wood, setting out). The axe is bronze-headed (I). Sarah is not shown: the text does not mention her in this chapter. 22:4: the first two days of travel are not pictured apart from D1 (I).

22:6: 'the fire' is a small clay firepot of embers and 'the sacrificial knife' a short bronze knife in a sheath at Abraham's belt (both I; flint was used in earlier units only for circumcision, from Exodus 4:25). The wood is carried on Isaac's back by rope loops.

22:9-10: nothing here goes beyond the text and no blow is shown. The binding is two pairs of hands and a cord (I4); Isaac lies clothed on the wood with his wrists tied, looking at the sky, and does not struggle (the text records no word or resistance from him; his calm is I). 22:10 'reached out his hand and took the knife' is painted exactly so: a hand closing on the handle of the knife where it lies on the altar stone (J1), Abraham's face (J2) and a distant figure with his arm lowered (J3). The knife is never shown raised over the boy. L1 (the knife fallen on the rock, the hand open) and L3 (the cord untied) are I: the text does not narrate either, but 22:12-13 require them.

22:13: the ram is a full-grown horned white ram in a thorn thicket behind Abraham. Its slaughter is not shown: Abraham frees it (M3), then the altar burns with nothing visible in the fire but wood (M4). M5 (the embrace) is D. 22:14 N2 shows the altar alone at sunset for 'to this day'.

22:17-18: the stars and the sand are shown as themselves; 'possess the gates of their enemies' is one faceless vision of an open city gate with people streaming in, no fighting (Q4); 'all nations of the earth' is a faceless multitude turned toward a light (R1). No nation, city or person is identified, and how the promise is fulfilled (Galatians 3:16 reads the offspring as Christ) is left to the later books.

22:19: the text says 'Abraham went back to his servants' and does not name Isaac here. He is painted coming down a step behind his father and travelling home with the party (I, from 22:5 'we will return to you'; nothing in the text says he stayed behind). Beersheba is the well and the tamarisk of 21:31-33, the tree now twice a man's height (I).

22:20-24: the bearer of the news is an unnamed traveller (I). Nahor and Milcah are the NAHOR_B and MILCAH of s01e03b grown old (description blocks, no sheets; I). Where they live is not named in this chapter and is painted only as a mud-brick house on a northern plain (I; 24:10 later speaks of 'the city of Nahor' in Aram-naharaim). The eight sons are shown as three (U1: Uz, Buz, Kemuel, with a small boy at Kemuel's knee for 'the father of Aram') and five (U2), each described singly so the count can be checked. Bethuel is the youngest in U2 and holds the newborn Rebekah in V1 (her age relative to Isaac is not given; I). Rebekah has no sheet here: Genesis 24 designs her. Reumah is shown with exactly four children (W1); Maacah is a wrapped baby because the name does not settle son or daughter. W2 (Isaac at the well, Abraham watching) is D, a turn toward Genesis 24.
Style line: 'tents of black goat hair' is left out of this episode's style (lesson of s02e01a) and tents are named only in the stills set at Beersheba.
